description: UK: how much of a defined contribution pension can be taken tax-free (2026/27). Usually 25% of each pot, capped by the lump sum allowance (£268,275 for life across all pensions, less any already used; the lower of what is left of the lump sum allowance and the lump sum and death benefit allowance). A disqualifying pension credit (from a divorce) does not support tax-free cash. Also gives the most PCLS for money moved into drawdown (one third of the amount designated). Reproduces GOV.UK's £60,000 pot example and HMRC PTM063240's Amanda, Mike and Tim examples. Use this when someone asks how much tax-free cash they can take from a UK pension.
